details: Brent crude oil prices dropped sharply after a reported pause in US strikes on Iran, pushing Brent below $90 a barrel. This de-escalation of geopolitical tensions has eased inflation concerns that previously increased the likelihood of a Federal Reserve rate hike. Markets are now adjusting expectations ahead of the Fed's July 29 interest rate decision, with the chance of a hike seen as lower, though the event is still expected to bring potential volatility.
title: Oil Plunge Eases Inflation Fears Ahead of Fed Rate Decision

details: Alongside the US Federal Reserve, the Bank of Japan (BoJ) and the Bank of England (BoE) are scheduled to announce their monetary policy decisions this week. A key concern for crypto markets is the BoJ's stance; while rates are expected to hold, a potential hike by year-end, combined with a weakening yen, could trigger an unwind of yen-denominated carry trades, potentially pressuring Bitcoin and DeFi liquidity.
title: BoJ & BoE Decisions Loom as Yen Weakness Poses Crypto Risk

details: US-listed spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs recorded combined net outflows of approximately $311 million on July 24, ending a seven-day streak of inflows. This shift in institutional flow, alongside a "Fear" reading on the Crypto Fear & Greed Index, reflects a cautious market sentiment among crypto investors as they await major macroeconomic announcements and navigate a period of consolidation for Bitcoin around $65,000.
title: Bitcoin ETFs See Net Outflows Amid Cautious Market Sentiment

details: Cryptocurrency exchange BitMEX announced it will shut down in September after 11 years of operation, with new user registrations halting immediately. The decision follows a strategic review of the business and the broader crypto industry. BitMEX was notable for pioneering perpetual swaps in 2016.
title: BitMEX Crypto Exchange Announces Closure After 11 Years
